title: Two Versions Behind, No More: The App Updates Itself | vitalii.no
description:
Why an Android app kept running two versions behind, and how it learned to install its own updates without ever asking for a tap.

Version 15 of the app had already been downloaded to the phone, but installing a sideloaded APK still required a manual tap that the owner never got around to. So every night, the drive ran on version 13, quietly missing whatever the newer build had fixed, with no way for the app itself to notice or close that gap.

A new Updater component, wired into the app's drive service and main activity, now checks for a newer version after every drive ends or whenever the app is opened. It downloads the APK, verifies both the package name and the version before touching anything, then installs it through Android's own PackageInstaller — which skips the confirmation prompt entirely once the app is registered as its own installer of record. It explicitly refuses to update while a drive is running, so a story never cuts out mid-playback for an install.

The phone now always carries whatever version was last shipped, with zero taps from the owner — closing a gap that used to run two versions deep.
